name: Beat drop on the product reveal

source.description: 1 inspected reference film (batch-7, 2026-11-26): a 47.6 s light SaaS launch tells its problem over a sparse bed and brings in the full beat, 7.3 dB louder, as the product fills the frame.

technique: The problem is told over a sparse, quiet intro; the full beat enters, louder and denser, at the moment the product's main interface fills the frame. The arrangement marks the turn from problem to solution without a cut or an added sound effect.
purpose: Mark the turn from problem to solution with the arrangement alone, without a cut or an added effect.
visual_behaviour: The problem plays over a sparse, quiet intro; at the moment the product's main window fills the frame the full beat enters and the film runs at full energy to the end.
mechanics: Intro bed about 7 dB below the body (median -24.6 dB against -17.3 dB) with onsets 0.2-1.0 s apart; at the turn the level steps up 7.3 dB within about 0.2 s (13.33 -> 13.51 s) and onsets go to every 0.11-0.23 s; the picture grows the main window to fill the frame across the step (11.0-13.97 s).

decomposition.timing: Intro about 13 s of a 47.6 s film (28%); one step, no return.

parameters.name: introLevel
parameters.description: Intro bed level relative to the body, dB

parameters.name: stepAt
parameters.description: The moment the product fills the frame

failure_modes: A step on a non-event reads as a mix error
Under narration the step must be ducked so the voice stays on top

implementation.approach: Choose or edit a bed with a sparse intro section, or automate its level in the mix: intro about 7 dB under the body, a step up within about 0.2 s on the frame the product fills the screen (snap it with studio.py words in a narrated film), no return. Under narration duck the body so the voice stays on top. Not built as a preset.

requirements: bed with an intro section or level automation

provenance.observed: Sparse intro under the problem and first feature (0-13.4 s, median -24.6 dB); at 13.42 s the full beat enters, +7.3 dB, as the calendar window fills the frame; the body stays at about -17.3 dB to the end.

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
